title: Frontend offers the whole saved address book on every consignment party picker, so a consignee page lists farms of origin; Design release 1 offers only the addresses saved for that party

finding.frontend: Every one of Frontend's five party pickers offers the same list. The place-of-origin picker and the consignee picker are identical in the captured DOM: both are captioned "Showing 5 of 13 addresses" and both offer Astra Rosales, Tech Imports Ltd, Origin Farm, British Livestock Ltd and Import Co UK, in that order, with the remaining eight behind pagination. So the page that asks for the farm the animals left offers UK importers, and the page that asks who is receiving them offers foreign farms. This is by design and not a fixture accident: Frontend's address book holds no address type at all — "Addresses have no type in the address book (D3) — the same record may be a consignor on one notification and a consignee on the next. So every picker searches one book, and no function here takes a role" (src/server/app/services/address-book/index.js:12-15) — and the picker controller calls the book with a query and a page number and nothing else (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/party-picker/party-picker.controller.js:36). No amount of real data changes what these pages offer, because there is no field to filter on.
finding.prototype: Design release 1 offers a party picker only the saved addresses whose type matches that party, and the two captured pickers show it: the place-of-origin picker says "Showing 9 out of 9 results" over nine farms in Romania, the Republic of Ireland, the Netherlands, Austria and Poland; the consignee picker offers six UK companies — Northern Livestock Imports Ltd, West Coast Animal Imports Ltd, East Midlands Animal Imports Ltd, Britannia Trade & Livestock Ltd, Prime Livestock UK Ltd and GB Animal Trade Services Ltd — and no farms. The list is filtered on the address's own type against the type the section implies (app/routes.js:3457-3466), which is the same seven-value type every saved address carries in the address book. A newly added address only appears in the section it was added for, because the same match runs over the additions too.
finding.difference: Two pieces, in order. Saved addresses need a type — the address book API's locked wire contract carries no type or role field on an address (OperatorResponse in trade-imports-address-book), so this cannot be done in Frontend alone and the band is needs-backend: the contract needs a type, or a set of types, per address, and whichever service writes the book needs to ask for it. Then Frontend's address-book service needs to take a role — today search and all take a query and a page and nothing else (src/server/app/services/address-book/index.js:12-15) — and each picker needs to pass the role its section implies. The order matters: until the contract carries the type there is nothing to filter on, and a Frontend-only fix would have to guess a party's role from its name. Note that this is a live defect in the notification journey whichever way the address-book scope question (address-book--saved-address-book-pages-absent) is settled, because it is about what the pickers already show rather than about pages Frontend does not have. controls is empty deliberately: the finding is which rows the results list contains, and the whole-page shot is the picture that shows it — cropping any one control would show less.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding a role, type or section argument on any call into Frontend's address-book service, or two Frontend party pickers that offer different rows for the same search. The place-of-origin and consignee pickers were captured independently and their result tables are identical row for row.
finding.verification: Written and checked by the verifier, not by the slice's author — a reader should know both halves are mine. Found it by asking rubric 5 of the address-book slice: the author had folded the seven address types into a disputed finding's difference slot, where they would be struck along with it, so I checked whether the types bite anywhere Frontend already renders. They do. Compared the captured DOM of fe-address-picker-place-of-origin.html and fe-address-picker-consignee.html — both caption "Showing 5 of 13 addresses" and both list the same five names in the same order — against dr1-consignment-address-select.html (nine placeOfOriginAddressId rows) and dr1-consignment-address-select-consignee.html (six consigneeAddressId rows, no overlap of names). Read app/routes.js:3457-3466 to confirm Design release 1 filters on the address type rather than shipping a separate fixture list per section, and app/routes.js:3520-3542 to confirm the same match is applied to session-added addresses. Read src/server/app/services/address-book/index.js:12-15 and party-picker.controller.js:36 for the Frontend side, and checked the address-book API's OperatorResponse record field by field: no type, role or category field on the wire, which is what sets the band to needs-backend rather than frontend-work. Checked this is not a fixture difference under the contract's own test — swapping the stub for real data leaves it exactly where it is, because there is no field to filter on.

relatedTo.why: The seven address types Design release 1's address book asks for on its add form are the same types these pickers filter on; that finding enumerates them, this one is the part of them that is already visible inside the notification journey.
